description: The WhatsApp operator routes (WhatsAppController, found by the V1-21b final repair with AuthGuard and BusinessGuard only) no longer leak or let any member change the business's sending identity. GET /whatsapp/businesses/:b/config answers no secret value to anyone: provider and fromNumber, and each credential (accessToken, authToken, accountSid) as {configured, last4}, last4 and phoneNumberId only for a member who may write the config. PATCH .../config is OWNER only (owner ruling D-11: the business profile, its sending identity and sibling business-config writes): the OWNER membership or Business.ownerId, plus the SUPER_ADMIN bypass, bound to the route's business; anyone else gets 403 {code:'BUSINESS_PROFILE_OWNER_ONLY'} (the code every D-11 writer answers) with the Business row byte-identical. A PATCH that omits a credential, sends it blank or mask-shaped, or echoes the GET view back keeps the stored ciphertext; a submitted credential that is already ciphertext (enc:v1:, e.g. another business's stored token) is refused 400 {code:'WHATSAPP_CREDENTIAL_CIPHERTEXT'} and a phoneNumberId another business holds (the shared webhook's routing key) is refused 409 {code:'WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID_IN_USE'}, nothing written, the claim serialised by an advisory lock on the id. POST send and POST messages need operations:write; GET status, conversations, conversations/:id, templates and POST test need operations:read (the module key KeyInboxController requires); the config owner (WhatsAppService.isConfigOwner, incl. a distinguished owner with no membership row) passes them too (WhatsAppOperationsScopeGuard). GET status carries phoneNumberId (as platformId) only to a config writer. A foreign business answers 403 with nothing written; the four webhook handlers are unchanged (no guards). No provider traffic: sends use the mock provider, global fetch is a failing recorder. R0-SEC2b-WHATSAPP-SECRET-READS extends it: the Business reads (GET /identity/businesses/:id, GET /identity/businesses, the PATCH response and the business POST /identity/bootstrap answers, all through sanitizeBusiness) answer metaData.whatsapp as {configured} only, to every reader, the owner included (no credential plaintext or ciphertext, no phoneNumberId); PATCH /identity/businesses/:id refuses a metaData.whatsapp key 400 {code:'BUSINESS_METADATA_KEY_RESERVED'} with nothing written (saveConfig is its only writer); the D-11 static guard lists metaData.whatsapp (D11W-09) and reports a caller's bag merged into metaData anywhere as opaque metaData that must be allow-listed (D11W-10). R0-SEC2c-PAYMENT-SECRETS-WRITE-ONLY extends it to the payment provider secrets Business.metaData carries (stripeSecretKey, stripeWebhookSecret, paypalClientSecret, wipayApiKey): every Business read (GET /identity/businesses/:id, GET /identity/businesses, the PATCH response, the POST /identity/bootstrap business, all through sanitizeBusiness) answers each as {configured:true} only, to every reader BusinessGuard admits (a blank or null stored value reads as absent), and the stored row is unchanged by a read; on PATCH /identity/businesses/:id a secret is written only when a new non-blank string is sent (trimmed), an omitted, blank or mask-shaped value keeps the stored one, an explicit null removes the key, and the write stays OWNER only (D-11). Run from apps/server against this packet's isolated, migrated database: npx vitest run test/whatsapp-config-authority.integration.test.ts test/whatsapp.controller.test.ts src/core/config/d11-owner-writes.spec.ts test/payment-secrets-write-only.integration.test.ts
notes: The owner rule is restated in WhatsAppService.isConfigOwner (WhatsAppModule does not import IdentityModule), as TemplatesService.isProfileOwner, FinanceSettingsService and GmailService.assertConnectAuthority restate it: the OWNER membership, Business.ownerId and the SUPER_ADMIN platform bypass. PATCH config keeps AuthGuard + BusinessGuard and runs assertConfigOwner first; ModuleScopeGuard is not put on the config routes because it refuses a distinguished owner with no membership row (R0-CMF5 notes).

Module key: 'operations', the key every KeyInboxController route requires (WhatsApp inbound is ingested into the KEY inbox). Role defaults: STAFF operations:read (reads, no send), ADMIN and OWNER admin. The scoped routes run WhatsAppOperationsScopeGuard, a ModuleScopeGuard subclass that first admits WhatsAppService.isConfigOwner for the route's business (review CR-SEC2-1: ModuleScopeGuard alone refused the distinguished owner with no membership row the send and inbox routes, while PATCH config admitted it); everyone else gets ModuleScopeGuard's answer unchanged. The KEY inbox routes themselves still refuse that owner (ModuleScopeGuard, outside this write set).

phoneNumberId stays plain at rest: the shared webhook routes inbound by metaData.whatsapp.phoneNumberId. The three credentials stay encrypted with core/crypto/token-crypto encryptToken as before; a kept credential is the stored ciphertext, not re-encrypted.

R0-SEC2b: the d11-owner-writes static guard lists metaData.whatsapp in OWNER_ONLY_META_KEYS with WhatsAppService.saveConfig (guard assertConfigOwner) as its one writer, and pins that IdentityService.updateBusiness consults PROFILE_PATCH_RESERVED_META_KEYS before its write (D11W-09), proven on the real database by SEC2-T02/T06. Review SEC2b-R2: the reader took every identifier spread inside metaData to copy the stored metaData and skipped any other non-literal spread, so a new caller-bag merge (`{ ...meta, ...extra }`, `{ ...meta, ...input.extra }`) in any service was invisible. It now follows a spread (or a non-literal metaData value) to its source: a `.metaData` read off a value that is not the caller's, or a call over such reads only, copies the stored metaData; a parameter, a name destructured from one, a property of either, a local holding one or a computed key is opaque metaData (metaData.<opaque>) and needs an allow-list entry (D11W-02). The review's probe is reproduced in memory by D11W-10 (it found nothing before the repair). In the tree that is updateBusiness (the profile PATCH, reserved keys refused first), OnboardingConciergeService.awardSetupMilestone (the computed `${milestone}At`, owner-guarded) and CaseStudyService.saveMeta (a private helper spreading its `meta` parameter; D11W-10 checks every caller passes the stored metaData loadMeta read).

Review SEC2-R1: encryptToken returns an 'enc:v1:' value unchanged and one platform key decrypts every business's ciphertext, so saveConfig refuses submitted ciphertext; only plaintext or the business's own kept ciphertext is written. Closed by R0-SEC2b (SEC2-T02, SEC2-T06): PATCH /identity/businesses/:id, which merges the caller's metaData bag, refuses a metaData.whatsapp key (present at all, null and the masked read included) 400 BUSINESS_METADATA_KEY_RESERVED before anything is read or written; a non-owner still gets the D-11 owner refusal (403) first (SEC2-T07).

Review SEC2-R3: the phoneNumberId uniqueness check uses the shared webhook's own predicate (business.findFirst on metaData.whatsapp.phoneNumberId; the soft-delete extension excludes deleted businesses); re-saving the id the business already stores is never refused, so a duplicate that predates the check does not lock its holder out. Making the webhook lookup deterministic for such pre-existing duplicates is left to V1-21b (the webhook handlers are unchanged here, SEC2-H01/H02).

Follow-ups closed by R0-SEC2b: SEC2-T01/T04/T05 (review SEC2-R2: sanitizeBusiness masks metaData.whatsapp as {configured}), SEC2-T02/T06 (identity PATCH refuses metaData.whatsapp), SEC2-T03 (review CR-SEC2-2: the web WhatsApp page and the Key Connect manage drawer render a 403 from GET status as no access and read the masked status; proven in jsdom by apps/web/src/app/app/whatsapp/__tests__/whatsapp-status-access.test.tsx, which this server-side manifest cannot bind).

Closed by R0-SEC2c-PAYMENT-SECRETS-WRITE-ONLY (R0-SEC2b review SEC2b-R3): Business.metaData also carries the payment gateway secrets the web payments tab writes (stripeSecretKey, stripeWebhookSecret, paypalClientSecret, wipayApiKey). RED-BEFORE census (SEC2c-R01): a STAFF member on role defaults, a STAFF member granted settings:write, an ADMIN, the owner, a co-owner, the distinguished owner (no membership) and a SUPER_ADMIN each received all four values from GET /identity/businesses/:id; the list, the PATCH response and the bootstrap answer carried them too. sanitizeBusiness now masks each as {configured:true} (BUSINESS_META_PAYMENT_SECRET_KEYS; a blank or null stored value is left out, so the commerce hooks that test these keys for truthiness keep their meaning) and IdentityService.updateBusiness applies the write-only rule (applyPaymentSecretWrites). The payment services read the secrets straight from Prisma, never through a Business read, so they are unaffected.

R0-SEC2c web half: apps/web/src/app/app/settings/business/payments-tab.tsx never holds a stored secret (it reads the {configured} marker, and an older server's plaintext as configured without showing it), shows Configured with Replace and Remove, and on save sends a secret only when the user typed one (null for Remove). Proven in jsdom by apps/web/src/app/app/settings/business/payments-tab.spec.tsx (SEC2c-UI01..UI05), which this server-side manifest cannot bind.

R0-SEC2c review SEC2c-ST-1 (lost update on Business.metaData): IdentityService.updateBusiness now locks the business row (SELECT ... FOR NO KEY UPDATE, as GmailService does) and reads and writes it in one transaction, so two profile PATCHes in flight no longer write a cleared or rotated secret back over each other (SEC2c-C01) and the PATCH no longer drops a key another writer committed meanwhile (SEC2c-C02). NOT closed (outside this write set, it.todo SEC2c-C03): the public POST /site/businesses/:businessId/analytics/event (SiteService.trackEvent) and about twenty other metaData writers read without the lock and write their whole copy back, so one that read before an owner's clear or rotation and writes after it still writes the old secret back; the follow-up is for those writers to merge their own key in the database (jsonb_set or ||) or take the same row lock.
